```markdown
# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion (specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md)

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md (§3 R1–R11 as outcome candidates; ranked by your partner, 2026-11-10). Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). | uv workspace of four packages (root `pyproject.toml`). | Azure platform per the ADR, status Proposed (2026-10-05).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A baseline filing-index catalog built from archived quarterly indexes over a range you choose (R1) | A | 1 | About 2 SEC requests per quarter (listing + index), under 1 s each at 3 req/s (§4.8). Bytes per quarter measured by Stage 1. Total scales with the range, which is not yet chosen. |
| O2 | Daily indexes ingested on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs (R2) | A | 2 | About 250 daily index files a year plus listings (one per business day). Bytes per file measured by Stage 1. |
| O3 | Indexes parsed, validated and normalized into canonical filing-index rows (R3) | A | 3 | Compute measured by Stage 1 (elapsed time, peak memory per quarter). |
| O4 | The pipeline running on Azure managed services: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor (R4) | A | 4 | Azure spend is unknown until Stage 7 deploys. The spec makes no cost claim before measurement (§2.2). |
| O5 | One downloader, parser and publisher shared by backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation (R5) | A | 5 | No separate cost. |
| O6 | Reprocessing from stored original bytes without downloading again (R6) | A | 6 | Storage grows by one raw copy per distinct snapshot. Size measured by Stage 1. |
| O7 | Periodic reconciliation of quarterly indexes that records later changes (R7) | A | 7 | One full re-read of every supported quarter each week (§4.8). Requests ≈ O1's per-quarter figure × quarters in range. |
| O8 | All SEC traffic under one request budget, however many workers run (R8) | A | 8 | Capped at 3 req/s by default (§4.8). The cap bounds the backfill's wall-clock time. |
| O9 | Readers get complete quarter generations through one active pointer (R9) | A | 9 | One retained generation per publish per quarter. Retention is a deployment value (§4.8). |
| O10 | Removed records leave the catalog only after approval tied to the source hash (R10) | A | 10 | Your time: one review per withdrawal candidate. Frequency is unknown until reconciliation runs. |
| O11 | Stated defaults for schedules, retries and request rate, changed only through config review (R11) | A | 11 | No separate cost. |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression). There is one track, by your partner's decision.

## Open questions

1. **Package layout.** §4.9 places all of this code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The repo also has scaffolds for `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, and a root script `sec-edgar = "sec_edgar:main"` that points at no module. Which package holds this work? Are the others kept, removed, or reserved for out-of-scope work (§2.2)? This gates Stage 1.
2. **Acceptance.** The ADR and the spec are both PROPOSED, and §7 step 1 makes acceptance the first step. Proposed default: Stages 1–6 build platform-neutral code, and acceptance gates Stage 7.
3. **Deployment values (§7 step 1).** Proposed default: the SEC identity (User-Agent) is set before Stage 1. The backfill range and the daily handoff date are set before Stage 8.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter and one real day to canonical rows
      Objective: Download one archived quarterly master index and one already published daily master index from the SEC, and parse both into canonical rows (§4.5 row contract).
      Outcomes: O1 (one quarter), O3
      Consumes: the workspace scaffold; answers to Open questions 1 and 3 (SEC identity)
      Produces: a parser that writes canonical rows to local Parquet for both index kinds, with raw bytes kept on disk; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one real quarter's rows exist in local Parquet beside its original bytes. O3 — rows from both files satisfy the §4.5 row contract, and a malformed row fails the run rather than being dropped. The findings file records byte count, row count, elapsed time, peak memory and SEC request count for each file.
      Leaves out: content-addressed snapshots and replay → Stage 2; range enumeration and golden fixtures across the range → Stage 2; discovery and catch-up → Stage 3; shared request budget, retry policy and config validation → Stage 4; generations, manifest and active pointer → Stage 5; reconciliation and withdrawal gate → Stage 6; Azure, observability and runbooks → Stage 7; production backfill and triggers → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Shared collector, snapshots and replay over a quarter range
      Objective: Backfill an inclusive quarter range through one collector and parser, keeping content-addressed raw snapshots and observations so that a parser change replays without SEC requests (§4.2 Backfill, §4.3 Validation, §4.5 paths and source manifest).
      Outcomes: O1 (range), O5, O6
      Consumes: Stage 1 parser and findings
      Produces: a `collect`/`transform` path shared by both index kinds; the source/snapshot/processing manifest on a local store; golden fixtures for the formats in the chosen range
      Exit: O1 — a multi-quarter backfill reports complete, pending and failed units separately. O5 — quarterly and daily inputs go through the same collector and parser. O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds observations from stored bytes with zero SEC requests, and unchanged hashes skip work.
      Leaves out: discovery via listings and catch-up → Stage 3; shared lease and throttling → Stage 4; quarter generations and pointer → Stage 5; ADLS and Table Storage backends → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Daily discovery and catch-up
      Objective: Discover daily and quarter-to-date sources from `index.json` listings and catch up across missed runs and quarter boundaries (§4.2 Daily ingestion, §5 Discovery and Not yet available).
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 2 collector and manifest
      Produces: a `discover` command and a durable discovery boundary that pending and failed sources survive
      Exit: O2 — the §6 Discovery and coverage cases pass, including an outage that spans quarters, a failed listing that does not advance the boundary, and a `no_new_sources` report.
      Leaves out: scheduled triggers → Stage 8; the baseline/daily overlap at the production handoff date → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: One SEC request budget and stated defaults
      Objective: Put every SEC request behind one renewable lease, a rate target and a bounded retry policy, with configuration validated before any I/O (§4.3 One request budget, §4.8, §5 Configuration, Throttled, Access blocked, Ownership lost).
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stages 2–3 collector and discovery
      Produces: a lease-guarded downloader; typed configuration with the §4.8 defaults
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors under test never overlap as request issuers, retries count toward the budget, and a 403 halts access. O11 — invalid or out-of-ceiling configuration is refused before any network request, and every §4.8 key has its stated starting value.
      Leaves out: the Storage-backed lease on Azure → Stage 7; ADF-owned schedules → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Quarter generations and the active pointer
      Objective: Publish each affected quarter as an immutable generation with a manifest and change report, committed by a conditional pointer update (§4.6 Publish, §4.5 Quarter publication).
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 2 observations and manifest
      Produces: a `publish` command; a pointer store with conditional writes, behind an interface that Stage 7 backs with Table Storage
      Exit: O9 — the §6 Publication cases pass: injected crashes before files finish, before the pointer moves and just after it moves; competing publishers lose no update; readers see only complete generations.
      Leaves out: the withdrawal gate → Stage 6; Table Storage and ADLS backends → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and the withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly sources, apply the §4.4 precedence rules, publish safe changes, and hold withdrawals for hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stages 2–5
      Produces: a reconciliation workflow; withdrawal approval records; the `awaiting_approval` outcome
      Exit: O7 — additions and field updates publish with recorded before/after values. O10 — the §6 Reconciliation cases pass: open-quarter absence never withdraws, a closed-quarter removal waits for approval of its exact hash, and stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key.
      Leaves out: the weekly trigger → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment in an isolated environment
      Objective: Run the shared worker as Container Apps Jobs orchestrated by ADF, on ADLS and Table Storage, with Monitor logs and alerts, IaC, managed identities and runbooks (§4.1, §4.7, §4.9, §6 Orchestration and Integration tests, §7 steps 2–5, §8).
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–6; Open question 2 resolved (ADR and spec accepted)
      Produces: versioned infrastructure with triggers disabled; a pinned image digest; runbooks; the smoke-test record
      Exit: O4 — integration tests pass on isolated Azure resources; a live smoke test of one quarter and one daily index records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest and request rate; a replay from raw storage with SEC access disabled matches.
      Leaves out: production backfill and trigger enablement → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline campaign and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill, catch daily ingestion up from the handoff date, run reconciliation once, then enable triggers and observe scheduled runs (§7 steps 6–9, §10).
      Outcomes: O1 (production baseline), O2 (scheduled), O7 (scheduled)
      Consumes: Stage 7 deployment; the backfill range and handoff date (Open question 3)
      Produces: a release record naming the image, the configuration and the active quarter generations; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-8-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — every requested quarter is published, or the incomplete range is approved and recorded. O2 — daily runs observed on schedule against their durable reports. O7 — weekly reconciliation observed on schedule with gated candidates resolved. The findings file records the backfill's bytes, elapsed time and request rate.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O11 against the accumulated system, with evidence per verdict (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred items). An unmet outcome exits as a new stage or as a recorded deferral with its reason. Then retire this roadmap to specs/completed/.
```
